pages.text: Morning sunlight filled Kiki's burrow entrance. Moya tapped their hooves outside. "Kiki, sunrise! Let's get water!" The meerkat curled up inside, tail tucked. "A little longer... It's so cozy here."
Moya tapped the dirt, but Kiki wouldn't move. "Go first. I'll sleep a little more." Kiki snored again. Moya's hoofbeats faded, and the sun climbed higher.
Kiki woke with a start. The sun was already in the middle of the sky! Footprints crowded the waterhole, and the water was yellow with mud. "Already?" Kiki pouted.
Kiki scooped a sip with their paws. "Ptoo! It tastes like dirt!" Wildebeests and zebras had already drunk there. Kiki's paws drooped. "I wanted clear water..."
Mom gently nudged Kiki's back. "The first morning water is clearest. After everyone drinks, it gets muddy. So sunrise—off to the water!"
Mom whispered, "Getting up isn't hard. Come outside at sunrise and stand on two feet. Warm your tummy in the sun, and you'll wake right up." Kiki looked up, wanting to meet the sun.
Next morning, sunlight filled the entrance. Kiki popped out and stood tall, chest open. A warm tummy chased sleep away. "Hello, morning! Sunrise—off to the water!"
The water was clear as a mirror, reflecting blue sky. Kiki scooped and drank. Cool and sweet! "The first morning water!" Moya laughed. "You're earlier than me today!"
Now Kiki knew the steps. "One, out at sunrise! Two, stand and warm up in the sun! Three, race to the first water!" The following morning, Kiki was outside before Moya called.
Mom nuzzled Kiki's cheek. "Up bright as the morning sun!" Going to the water at sunrise meant clear water to drink. Sunrise—off to the water!
